extracted.intended_audience: insurance industry readers and regulatory observers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and ensuring the integrity of public notice-and-comment submissions (authenticity, consent, and lawful advocacy practices) and identifying abusive practices that corrupt rulemaking. Focuses on detecting fabricated comments, improper use of consumer identities, and required reforms/enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect integrity of public comment process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Public comment opportunities are a chance for Americans to give their input on important government policies," (and) should reflect genuine public input rather than manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should represent authentic views of real individuals and not be co-opted by companies to advance private agendas. The OAG framed abuse of the process as using public comment opportunities for selfish purposes, undermining rulemaking legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use identities without knowledge or consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The fake comments "used the identities of millions of consumers, including thousands of New Yorkers, without their knowledge or consent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting comments or using consumer identities requires authorization; impersonation or use of personal data without consent is abusive and can trigger investigation and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit fabrication of consumer responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators "simply fabricated consumers’ responses" instead of enrolling real consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generating comments by inventing responses or manufacturing submissions is prohibited; organisers and vendors must ensure every comment/letter reflects an actual person's stated view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine enrollment practices when using lead generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators used advertisements and prizes to encourage consumers to join campaigns but often fabricated enrollments instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lead generators or third-party vendors are used, they must genuinely enroll and verify consumers rather than substitute fabricated responses; incentive mechanisms (gift cards, sweepstakes) must not mask or motivate fraudulent submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a false impression of popular support
rubrics_metrics.description: The fabricated comments provided "cover" for the FCC to repeal net neutrality rules and created a false impression of popular support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy campaigns must not manufacture apparent grassroots backing through fake comments, mass-produced letters, or automated/signature fraud intended to mislead regulators about public sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose funding and avoid secret campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Report said the nation’s largest broadband companies funded a "secret campaign" to generate millions of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers and sponsors should be transparent about who is funding or coordinating comment campaigns; secrecy about funding or orchestration that masks centralized or paid efforts can mislead agencies and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent cross-proceeding contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation found the fraud "infected other government proceedings as well," generating fake comments for multiple agencies and officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors and campaign organizers must not reuse fabricated tactics across different rulemakings, petitions, or legislative correspondence; safeguards should prevent fraudulent submissions in any proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify authenticity of digital signatures and petition signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 3.5 million fake digital signatures for letters and petitions were generated for federal and state legislators and government officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When collecting e-signatures or petition signatures for advocacy, verify that signatures are tied to real individuals and are not mass-fabricated or spoofed; lack of verification opens campaigns to fraud allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet intermediaries and subcontracted vendors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ifficient acted as an intermediary, engaging other lead generators and supplied its client with more than 840,000 fake responses it had received from the lead generators it had hired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients must exercise due diligence when hiring intermediaries or subcontractors (lead generators); monitor their practices and require accountability to ensure responses are genuine and not fabricated by downstream vendors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement comprehensive reforms in future advocacy campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements with the OAG required the companies to "adopt comprehensive reforms in future advocacy campaigns."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firms implicated in abusive comment practices are expected to change procedures (e.g., verification, transparency, vendor oversight). Although specific reforms are not detailed here, enforcement settlements can mandate procedural safeguards and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and financial accountability for fraudulent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectively, the three companies have agreed to pay $615,000 in penalties and disgorgement; prior agreements required over $4.4 million in penalties and disgorgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting fabricated comments can trigger investigations, civil enforcement, and monetary penalties. Organizations should weigh legal and reputational risks and ensure compliance to avoid fines and other sanctions.
